## PSY 0210 extension: conditions-validation script

*(0110 students: optional/ungraded — feel free to attempt this for practice, but it is not required and does not affect your grade.)*

Per class04, write a **standalone Python script** — not a Builder file, not a Colab notebook, run on its own via PsychoPy's Coder view — that validates your own conditions spreadsheet against this course's ≥18-observations-per-condition rule.

**Start from the template, don't write this from scratch.** Reading a file from disk and handling command-line arguments are genuinely new skills this course doesn't otherwise teach — so `hw2/check_conditions_template.py` already has that part written and explained. Copy it to `hw2/task/check_conditions.py` and fill in only the part marked `TODO`: counting how many trials each condition produces and printing a pass/fail line for each one. That counting logic is the same dictionary-counting pattern from class04's Colab warm-up — same idea, just counting rows in a spreadsheet instead of items in a list.

**Submit it as `hw2/task/check_conditions.py`.** (This exact filename and path is what the automated check looks for — if you name it something else, the 0210 portion of the check will simply be skipped, so use this path.)

The template already handles:

- Reading your conditions spreadsheet with `pandas` (`.xlsx` or `.csv`).
- Accepting the conditions file path as an optional command-line argument, falling back to a default path you set at the top of the file for your own local testing. This is what lets you just click PsychoPy Coder's **Run** button with no changes, *and* lets the automated check point the same script at a small sample file instead of your real data.
- A clear error message if the file it's pointed at doesn't exist.

Your job is filling in the `TODO` section so the script:

1. Counts how many trials each condition will produce once repetitions are applied (rows × `N_REPS`, already a constant near the top of the file).
2. Prints a clear pass/fail message **per condition** against the ≥18-observations-per-level rule, e.g.:

   ```
   congruent: 18 trials — OK
   incongruent: 12 trials — FAILS minimum of 18
   ```

The automated check runs `python check_conditions.py sample_conditions.csv` against a small synthetic sample conditions file (not your real data) and only confirms it runs without crashing and prints output — it does not check your exact wording or verify your pass/fail logic is correct. The sample file has the same columns as the original Stroop conditions file (`word`, `letterColor`, `corrAns`, `congruent`, plus a `condition` column), so as long as your `CONDITION_COLUMN` is one of those names the sample will have it; if your own modified conditions file uses a column name of your own invention, the automated check can't find that column and will report a red X even though your script may be fine — mention that in your reflection and don't worry about it. One more rule: **print your pass/fail lines rather than exiting with an error code** (no `sys.exit(1)` on a failed condition) — the sample file deliberately contains a failing condition, and the automated check treats any non-zero exit as a crash. Getting the logic right against your own real conditions file is on you; test it yourself against your conditions spreadsheet before submitting.
